title: Integrated Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2026 Q1)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard procedures for annual and quarterly budgeting, procurement approvals, contract lifecycle management, and revenue recognition and billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, sales, and engineering teams that engage external vendors, sign customer agreements, or own P&L responsibilities.

Scope:
- Budgeting and forecasting (annual and rolling quarterly updates)
- Procurement lifecycle and approval thresholds
- Contract review and execution process (MSA, SOW, reseller/partner agreements)
- Revenue recognition (ASC 606-aligned summary) and billing practices
- Exceptions, audits, and escalation paths

Owners and Key Contacts:
- Finance: Head of FP&A (primary owner) — responsible for budget consolidation, forecasting cadence, and revrec guidance
- Legal: Commercial Counsel — contract templates, clause guidance, and exceptions approvals
- Procurement: Procurement Manager — vendor onboarding and purchase order (PO) issuance
- Sales & Billing: Billing Manager — invoicing cadence, billing disputes, and collections

Definitions and Principles:
- Materiality thresholds: For budget and procurement controls, see Approval Matrix below.
- ASC 606 principles: Identify contract(s) with a customer; identify performance obligations; determine transaction price; allocate price to obligations; recognize revenue when obligations are satisfied.
- Principle of segregation of duties: Requester, Approver, and Payer roles must be distinct for transactions greater than $10,000.

Budgeting and Forecasting Process:
1) Annual Budget Calendar:
   - Sep–Oct: Department-level planning and headcount proposals submitted to FP&A
   - Nov: Cross-functional review and scenario modelling (base, upside, downside)
   - Dec 15: Executive review and finalized budget submission to Board
   - Jan 1: Budget goes live; monthly variance reporting begins
2) Rolling Forecasts:
   - FP&A publishes a rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly with inputs from sales, product, and engineering
   - Forecast variance tolerance: Finance escalates variances >5% quarter-over-quarter for core expense categories (cloud, infra, payroll)
3) Chargeback and Cost Allocation:
   - Central infrastructure and shared services are allocated to product teams using a transparent monthly cost allocation report. Methodology documented in the FP&A team repo.

Procurement and Purchase Approval Matrix:
- <$10,000: Requester manager approval; PO via procurement portal recommended but not required for repeat low-value purchases.
- $10,000–$50,000: Department head approval + Procurement review; vendor due diligence required (security questionnaire or SOC2 report).
- $50,001–$250,000: Director-level approval + Procurement and Legal intake; standard MSA required for multi-year or data-access vendors.
- >$250,000: VP-level approval + Procurement, Legal, and Finance sign-off; Procurement to run competitive review when applicable.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist:
- Complete vendor intake form in procurement portal
- Security review: request SOC2 or equivalent; if handling sensitive customer data, require security questionnaire and remediation plan
- Contract template selection: standard MSA where applicable; Escalate to Legal for non-standard terms
- PO issuance and 3-way match: PO -> goods/service receipt -> invoice before payment unless exceptions pre-approved

Contract Lifecycle and Review Process:
1) Contract Types and Templates:
   - Master Service Agreement (MSA): standard commercial terms, liability cap, IP assignment, confidentiality, data residency
   - Statement of Work (SOW): scope, milestones, acceptance criteria, and payment schedule
   - Reseller/Partner Agreements: revenue share, co-marketing, termination rights
   - Professional Services Agreement: time-and-materials or fixed-fee SOWs
2) Mandatory Legal Clauses Checklist:
   - Governing law and dispute resolution; preferred jurisdiction: Delaware for customer agreements, local law for certain international customers
   - Liability cap: default to lesser of 12 months of fees or $1M unless Legal-approved exception
   - Indemnification scope and limits
   - Data protection and security obligations; include audit rights for high-risk vendors
   - Confidentiality and return/destruction of data on termination
   - Export controls and sanctions representation
3) Review and Redline Process:
   - Submit initial contract via Legal intake form with commercial summary (value, term, renewal, customer/vendor risk)
   - Legal performs standard redline within 3 business days for routine contracts; expedited review SLA: 1 business day for pre-approved templates up to $50k
   - Non-standard terms escalate to Commercial Counsel and require documented risk acceptance if executed
4) Signature and Execution:
   - DocuSign is the standard execution platform. Contracts must be stored in the contract repository with metadata (counterparty, contract type, value, effective date, owner).

Revenue Recognition and Billing Policy (Summary):
- Accounting standard: ASC 606. Finance provides journal-entry templates and recognition schedules for common transaction types.
- Subscription ARR & Deferred Revenue:
   - Invoiced annual subscriptions: recognize revenue ratably over the contracted service period. Record deferred revenue on invoice date.
   - Monthly subscriptions: recognize revenue in the month service is provided.
- Usage-based billing:
   - Recognize revenue in the period the usage occurs. For metered usage billed in arrears, estimate and accrue revenue for the period based on usage reports if material.
- Professional services:
   - Fixed-fee with acceptance milestones: recognize on milestone acceptance dates.
   - Time & materials: recognize as services are performed.
- Variable consideration and estimates:
   - Apply constraint on variable consideration; use historical billing and contract terms to estimate rebates, credits, or usage variability.
   - Significant estimation methods must be documented and approved by Head of Accounting.
- Billing and Invoice Practices:
   - Standard payment terms: Net 30 unless altered by commercial negotiation and approved by Finance + Legal for deviations beyond Net 60
   - Invoicing cadence: monthly (usage/subscription), annual (prepaid enterprise contracts), or milestone-based per SOW
   - Late payment policy: 1.5% monthly interest after 30 days plus escalation to collections for invoices >90 days past due
   - Credits and refunds: require Finance approval; refunds >$10,000 require CFO sign-off
- SLA credits and revenue impact:
   - Credits issued for SLA violations are applied as billing credits; recognize impact to revenue according to ASC 606 guidance and record adjustments in the period the credit is approved

Journal Entry Examples (described):
- Prepaid annual subscription invoice: Debit Cash, Credit Deferred Revenue; monthly recognition: Debit Deferred Revenue, Credit Subscription Revenue
- Usage accrual (month-end estimate): Debit Accounts Receivable (accrued), Credit Revenue; reverse on invoice if invoice posts against AR

Controls, Audit, and Record Retention:
- Contract retention: all fully executed contracts retained for minimum 7 years in contract repository.
- Audit readiness: maintain supporting files for revenue recognition entries, including customer contracts, usage reports, and acceptance records.
- Internal controls: periodic 3-way match checks, segregation of duties for approvals, and monthly reconciliation of deferred revenue accounts by Finance.

Exceptions and Escalation:
- Non-standard legal terms, liability caps above policy, or commercial exceptions require documented risk assessment and approval by Legal and Finance; amounts >$250k also require executive sponsor approval.
- Procurement exceptions to PO or competitive bidding must be documented and approved by Procurement and Finance.

Quarterly Review and Continuous Improvement:
- Playbook review cadence: annually in Q4 and ad-hoc after material policy changes (accounting guidance, regulatory changes).
- Metrics tracked: budget variance %, days sales outstanding (DSO), percentage of contracts executed with standard MSA, average contract review time (SLA), number of vendor security exceptions.
